newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens buys 25 pct in car lock firms.
newsitem.headline: Siemens buys 25 pct in car lock firms.

text.p: German industrial giant Siemens AG said on Thursday it would acquire 25 percent of two German companies to boost its position in the market for keyless automobile locks.

Siemens would buy a quarter of Huelsbeck & Fuerst GmbH, a family-owned company with 24 million marks ($15.1 million) in capital and 600 million marks in 1996 sales. It would also take 25 percent of Huelsbeck & Fuerst partner Huf Industrieverwaltung GmbH.
Huelsbeck & Fuerst and Huf manufacture car door handles, steering wheel locks and other mechanical components for car entry systems. Together they have 2,600 employees.
Huf -- which has five production facilities in western Europe, two in the U.S. and three in Asia -- recently won its first orders from Ford Motor Co. and General Motors Corp .
Siemens' Automotive Systems (AT) group produces electronic security systems and generated four billion marks in sales last year. It has 15,000 employees.
The market for electronic locking and immobilisation systems should grow about 7.5 percent per year, driven by increasing demand for greater theft prevention, Siemens said.
